finding: A capped slice of a living graph either passes `--status --check` over text no round read, or can never pass again, and §5 does not say which. §5 makes `stale` the way a slice reopens when the graph changes ('a stale slice is not converged'), but it puts no staleness condition on the cap branch of `done` and reuses tp review's cap rules, and tp review waives staleness at the cap. A reached cap also refuses emission for good. A spec ends once, but a graph slice lives on: Workflow E's next topic routinely edits epics of milestones already reviewed. Reading 1 (as in tp review): after the cap, an edit to an epic of the slice gives `stale: true` with `--check` still 0, so Workflow E's gate passes over an unreviewed change. Reading 2 (stale also blocks cap-done): `--check` exits 1 and emission exits 4 forever, a dead end that only an operator raising `review_max_rounds` leaves. Two correct implementations disagree, and under either reading the slice gate does not mean what Workflow E uses it for.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §4 line 85: 'A cycle finding is one strongly connected component'; §3 lines 71-73: 'a write whose after-state holds an error the before-state did not exits 1 … so a file already holding an error is repaired one write at a time'. finding: Because a cycle finding is one SCC identified by its sorted ids, a write that shrinks a cycle without breaking it yields an error the before-state did not hold, and it is refused. So partial repair of a cycle is impossible one epic at a time, though §3 promises that 'a file already holding an error is repaired one write at a time'. Example: a↔b, c↔d, b→c, d→a form one SCC {a,b,c,d}. Every single-epic `set <id> depends_on=…` that removes edges leaves {c,d} or {a,b} as a cycle, a new identity, so it exits 1. Only a multi-epic `--bulk` replacement or `import --force` repairs it. The same holds for any rule a future implementation chooses to aggregate per file (for example one `dangling-reference` finding naming all sources): fixing one of two would be refused.
